current_action: Reporter generated final QA audit report.

planner_input.description: Autonomous smoke and assertion validations suite

project_analysis.summary: w3 schools is an educational website providing tutorials on various programming languages including Python.
project_analysis.main_purpose: To educate users about different programming languages through interactive tutorials and code examples.
expected_user_journey: Navigate to the Python tutorial page
Use the code editor to write and run code snippets

smoke_tests: Verify that the main navigation links (Home, Tutorials, References) are accessible.
Check if the Python tutorial page loads successfully.
regression_tests: Ensure that all sections of the Python tutorial page are functional and display correctly.
Validate that the code editor functions as expected.
boundary_tests: Test the behavior of the code editor with large input sizes.
Check if the system handles special characters in code snippets correctly.
negative_tests: Attempt to access non-existent tutorials or pages and verify error handling.
Submit invalid code snippets to the code editor and check for appropriate error messages.
accessibility_tests: Audit the website for compliance with WCAG 2.1 standards, focusing on navigation and content readability.
integration_tests: Verify that the code editor integrates seamlessly with the tutorial content.
Check if external resources (like libraries) can be imported and used in the code editor.
system_tests: Test the website's performance under high traffic conditions.
Ensure that the system handles concurrent users without crashing.
ui_tests: Perform visual checks on the layout, color scheme, and overall design of the website.
functional_tests: Verify that all interactive elements (like buttons, links) function as expected.
Check if the code editor provides accurate syntax highlighting and error messages.
exploratory_tests: Explore various parts of the website to identify any unexpected behavior or usability issues.
compatibility_tests: Test the website's compatibility with different browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
Verify that the website functions correctly on mobile devices and tablets.
security_tests: Perform security audits to identify any vulnerabilities in the code editor or tutorial content.
Check if the system handles user authentication securely.
performance_test_suggestions: Use tools like Lighthouse for performance benchmarking.
Test page load times under various network conditions.
api_test_suggestions: Identify any API endpoints used by the code editor and suggest load testing these endpoints.

user_workflow: Use code editor for hands-on practice

detected_modules.purpose: Provides educational material on various programming languages.

critical_user_journeys: Navigate to Python tutorial and run a code snippet
functional_requirements: The code editor should allow users to write and run Python code.
The tutorial content should be accurate and up-to-date.
non_functional_requirements: The website should load within 2 seconds on average.
The system should handle up to 100 concurrent users without performance degradation.
assertions: Validation message displayed for invalid code
explorer_instructions: Scan all interactive elements (buttons, links) on the page.
generator_instructions: Cover edge cases related to code editor functionality and performance.
validator_instructions: Verify that all critical success criteria are met for user navigation and interaction.
bug_analyzer_instructions: Capture console traces or network issues if validation fails.
reporter_instructions: Collect execution metrics such as page load times, error rates, and user interactions.

explorer_summary.summary: The page provides an introduction to Python programming and includes various interactive elements such as buttons, inputs, and forms. It also contains a large number of external links.

navigation_analysis.navigation_flow: The page has a linear navigation flow with multiple sections covering different aspects of Python programming.

<script>
activate_subtopnav_scroll = 0;
from_scrollpos = -1;
current_scrollpos = -1;
goto_tut = 1;
function startscrolling_subtopnav(event) {
  event.preventDefault();
  from_scrollpos = event.clientX;
  activate_subtopnav_scroll = 1;
}
function scrolling_subtopnav(event) {
  current_scrollpos = event.clientX;
  if (current_scrollpos == from_scrollpos) return false;
  event.preventDefault();
  if (event.buttons == 0) return false;
  var scrollspeed;
  if (activate_subtopnav_scroll == 1) {
    goto_tut = 0;
    scrollspeed = current_scrollpos - from_scrollpos;
    scrollspeed = Math.abs(scrollspeed);
    if (current_scrollpos < from_scrollpos) {
     document.getElementById("scroll_left_btn").style.display = "block";     
     document.getElementById("subtopnav").scrollLeft += scrollspeed;        
    } else {
      document.getElementById("subtopnav").scrollLeft -= scrollspeed;        
    }
    scrollbtn_visible();
    from_scrollpos = current_scrollpos;
  }
}
function endscrolling_subtopnav(event) {
  event.preventDefault();
  activate_subtopnav_scroll = 0;
  from_scrollpos = -1;
  current_scrollpos = -1;
}
function pellessii(event) {
  if (goto_tut == 0) {
    event.preventDefault();  
    goto_tut = 1;
    return false;
  }
}
var scrollspeed = 1;
var scrollinterval
function scrollmenow(n) {
  scrollinterval = window.setInterval(function() {
    scrollspeed = scrollspeed * 1.1;
    if (scrollspeed > 10) {scrollspeed = 10;}
    if (n == 1) {
      document.getElementById("subtopnav").scrollLeft += scrollspeed;  
    } else {
      document.getElementById("subtopnav").scrollLeft -= scrollspeed;  
      
    }
    scrollbtn_visible();
  }, 10);
}

var p_s_l = 0;
var x_s_l = 0;
function scrollbtn_visible() {
  var c_s_l = document.getElementById("subtopnav").scrollLeft;
  if (c_s_l < 1) {
    document.getElementById("scroll_left_btn").style.display = "none";    
  } else {
    document.getElementById("scroll_left_btn").style.display = "block";    
  }
  if (c_s_l > 1 && c_s_l == p_s_l) {
    x_s_l++;
  } else {
    x_s_l = 0;  
  }
  if (x_s_l > 3) {
    document.getElementById("scroll_right_btn").style.display = "none";    
  } else {
    document.getElementById("scroll_right_btn").style.display = "block";  
  }
  p_s_l = document.getElementById("subtopnav").scrollLeft;
}

function stopscrollmenow() {
  scrollspeed = 1;
  window.clearInterval(scrollinterval);
}

window.addEventListener("load", scrollbtn_visible);

function subtopnav_intoview() {
  var a, b, c, d, i = 0;
  a = document.getElementById("subtopnav");
  if (!a || !a.getElementsByClassName) {return false;}
  var x = a.getElementsByTagName("A");
  b = document.location.pathname;
  if (b.indexOf("/python/numpy/") > -1 || b.indexOf("/python/pandas/") > -1 || b.indexOf("/python/scipy/") > -1) {
    for (i = 0; i < x.length; i++) {
      c = x[i].pathname;
      if ((b.indexOf("/python/numpy/") > -1 && c == "/python/numpy/default.asp") || (b.indexOf("/python/pandas/") > -1 && c == "/python/pandas/default.asp") || (b.indexOf("/python/scipy/") > -1 && c == "/python/scipy/index.php")) {
        x[i].className += " active";
        break;
      }
    }
  } else {
    for (i = 0; i < x.length; i++) {
      c = x[i].pathname;
      if (c.indexOf("void(0)") == -1 && b.substr(0, b.indexOf("/",1)) ==  c.substr(0, c.indexOf("/",1))) {
        x[i].className += " active";
        break;
      }
    }
  }
  d = a.getElementsByClassName("active");
  if (d.length < 1) {return false;}  
  while (!amIIntoView(a, d[0])) {
    i++
    if (i > 1000) {break;}
    a.scrollLeft += 10;
    //console.log(i);
  }
  //scrollbtn_visible();
}

function amIIntoView(x, y) {
  var a = x.scrollLeft;
  var width = Math.min(window.innerWidth, 1750);
  var b = a + width - 20;
  var ytop = y.offsetLeft;
  var c = y.offsetWidth;
  var d = 0;
  if (document.getElementById("btn_container_subtopnav")) d = document.getElementById("btn_container_subtopnav").offsetWidth;
  var ybottom = ytop + c + d + 20;
  return ((ybottom <= b) && (ytop >= a));
}

<h2>What is Python?</h2>
<p>Python is a popular programming language. It was created by Guido van Rossum, 
and released in 1991.</p>

<p>It is used for:</p>

<ul>
<li>web development (server-side), </li>
<li>software development, </li>
<li>mathematics,</li>
<li>system scripting.</li>
</ul>

<h3>What can Python do?</h3>
<ul>
<li>Python can be used on a server to create web applications.</li>
<li>Python can be used alongside software to create workflows.</li>
<li>Python can connect to database systems. It can also read and modify files.</li>
<li>Python can be used to handle big data and perform complex mathematics.</li>
<li>Python can be used for rapid prototyping, or for production-ready software development.</li>
</ul>
<!--stop-->
<hr>
<!--start-->
<h2>Why Python?</h2>
<ul>
<li>Python works on different platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, Raspberry Pi, etc).</li>
<li>Python has a simple syntax similar to the English language.</li>
<li>Python has syntax that allows developers to write programs with fewer lines than some other programming languages.</li>
<li>Python runs on an interpreter system, meaning that code can be executed as soon as it is written. This means that prototyping can be very quick.</li>
<li>Python can be treated in a procedural way, an object-oriented way or a functional way.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Good to know</h3>
<ul>
<li>The most recent major version of Python is Python 3, which we shall be using in this tutorial.</li>
<li>In this tutorial Python will be written in a text editor. It is possible to write Python in an Integrated Development Environment, such as Thonny, Pycharm, Netbeans or Eclipse which are particularly useful when managing larger collections of Python files.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Python Syntax compared to other programming languages</h3>
<ul>
<li>Python was designed for readability, and has some similarities to the English language with influence from mathematics.</li>
<li>Python uses new lines to complete a command, as opposed to other programming languages which often use semicolons or parentheses.</li>
<li>Python relies on indentation, using whitespace, to define scope; such as the scope of loops, functions and classes. Other programming languages often use curly-brackets for this purpose.</li>
</ul>
